A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–B are readable and support a complete comparison. v4 retains the research material and appends a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v3 reports original goal-conditioned RL experiments, depth-scaling comparisons, architectural ablations, behavior analyses and runtime measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices A–B, including online and offline experiments, ablations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The contrastive RL objectives, residual architecture, normalization, activations and actor/critic scaling procedures are unchanged. The checklist introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten JaxGCRL environments, modified Ant U-Maze stitching scenario, OGBench offline tasks and additional FetchPush experiment. The checklist adds no evaluated task or domain.

E2.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the same original CRL, SAC, SAC+HER, TD3+HER, GCBC and GCSL comparators. Comparator participation in the additional scaling and architectural experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training budgets, model configurations, simulator versions and hyperparameters remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B. The checklist's seed disclosure does not establish a change in evaluation design.

E4.justification: The depth-versus-width, actor/critic, batch-size, architectural, exploration, representation, stitching and offline-scaling analyses retain the same evidence. No ablation, robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: v3 displays uncertainty without defining figure error bars or stating seed counts. v4 checklist item 7 specifies one standard error across random seeds, with five seeds for Figure 1 and three for other main-text figures. These are newly disclosed reporting details; they do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: The plotted outcomes, qualitative findings and performance/runtime tables are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Humanoid scores of 12.6 ± 1.3 at depth 4 and 649 ± 19 at depth 64. The checklist adds no experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: The goal-conditioned MDP definitions, discounted-visitation formulation, contrastive objectives and residual equations remain unchanged. The checklist adds no mathematical result, assumption, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the claims of scaling to 1024 layers, 2–50× CRL performance improvements and qualitatively different learned behaviors. Introduction edits and checklist summaries do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving exploration, expressivity and representations, the negative offline findings and the computational-cost limitation are unchanged. The checklist's latency statement reiterates the existing computational limitation.

D1.justification: The checklist newly states that reproduction documentation accompanies the code and discloses occasional LLM use for code debugging. These are limited disclosures; the code link, software versions, hyperparameters and timing information remain unchanged, and no new execution instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2, the scientific citations and the bibliography are unchanged. Checklist policy links do not alter the paper's relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited grammatical and wording corrections in the introduction, updates acknowledgments and funding, and appends a standardized checklist. The research narrative and ordering of existing sections and appendices remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds checklist pages with numbered questions and indented guideline lists, alongside local line reflow from prose edits. Existing figures, tables, captions, legends and their placement remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies previously undefined figure error bars and missing main-text seed counts, making the retained empirical evidence easier to assess. Together with small language corrections, this provides a limited reporting improvement; most checklist content reiterates existing material, and the scientific evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
